page: Amazon Web Services r7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. The platform is configured with 768 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 system memory, establishing an 8 GB per-thread allocation. Operating directly on bare metal without a virtualization hypervisor layer, the server provides low-latency execution and direct access to CPU hardware features, including 105 MB of shared L3 cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core.

Benchmark testing highlights top-tier multi-threaded compute and throughput capabilities, placing Geekbench multi-core results at 21623.0 and the overall PassMark CPU score at 88827.32, both within the top decile of evaluated systems. Hardware vector extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) accelerate complex math routines, reflected in prompt processing scores of 3005.64 tokens per second on 135M parameter language models and 294.37 tokens per second on 7B models. Memory subsystems demonstrate strong throughput, yielding 229.99 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations.

The server provides a 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, sustaining high transactional volumes such as 104.51 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 85.45 GB/sec static web serving throughput. A primary architectural consideration is the complete absence of integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data requirements. The instance delivers high resource density for workloads demanding vast RAM allocations and strong multi-core parallelism, proving suitable for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, software compilation pipelines, and CPU-bound matrix processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores on Intel Xeon 8488C processors clocked at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated hardware allocation and zero hypervisor overhead, it features 768 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier compute performance, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching 21623.0 and PassMark CPU scores reaching 88827.32, complemented by uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 229.99 GB/sec. The instance includes a 38 Gbps baseline network interface and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX for accelerated matrix operations. The server lacks onboard local storage, necessitating external storage volumes for stateful applications. It is suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, large-scale enterprise applications, high-throughput web serving, and extensive software compilation tasks.
